text:
sanjay: Heads-up — we've had 6 nodes with intermittent Xid errors last 48h, but the dmesg blobs we get are huge and often truncated in the kube logs. Need a compact extractor so triage is faster.

maria: +1. can we produce a 1-line summary per fault with context (Xid/ECC, pid, process, stack hint)?

ashley: agree. current plan: capture earliest kernel oops lines, last nvidia-smi error snapshot, and the last 100 journalctl -k lines surrounding the event. store as single artifact.

leo: rough command I used locally: 
```bash
# grab kernel lines with GPU keywords +/-100 lines around last occurrence
TS=$(journalctl -k --since "1 hour ago" | tac | grep -n "NVRM\|Xid" | head -n1 | cut -d: -f1)
if [ -n "$TS" ]; then journalctl -k --since "1 hour ago" | sed -n "$((TS-100)),$((TS+100))p"; fi
```

maria: can we produce a structured summary too? something like: [node, gpu-id, xid, ecc, last-pid, user, driver-version, sm-version]?

sanjay: yes — minimal JSON line per event for the catalog. example summary format we could append to S3: 
```json
{"node":"gpu-234","gpu":0,"xid":5,"ecc":"corrected","pid":4321,"comm":"python","driver":"535.54.03","time":"2026-02-12T10:12:03Z"}
```

ashley: for extraction heuristics: prioritize lines containing Xid, NVRM, ECCCORR, GPU fault, and 'GPU has fallen off the bus'. then include the nearest nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR snapshot.

infra-bot: FYI: added node-label gpu-triage=true when a drain is performed by ops. Use /triage-collect <node> to run the extractor (outputs tar.gz to /tmp and uploads to s3://redwood-gpu-triage).

leo: sample dmesg snippet we want captured (copied from node):
"[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (0001:04): 79, PID: 31245, 0x00000000a5b1c3f0
[ 1234.567895] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3d:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567900] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x%x)
"

maria: mapping table reminder for triage doc: Xid 31=ECC uncorrectable, 79=GPU fault/related to MMU, 63=thermal/drv mismatch; keep list in runbook.

ashley: also add ephemeral hook to capture nvml logs: 
```bash
# capture NVML error counters and process list on GPU
python - <<'PY'
from pynvml import *
nvmlInit()
for i in range(nvmlDeviceGetCount()):
  h=nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(i)
  print(i, nvmlDeviceGetName(h))
  try:
    err=nvmlDeviceGetDetailedEccErrors(h, NVML_SINGLE_BIT_ECC, NVML_VOLATILE_ECC)
    print('ecc', err)
  except Exception as e:
    print('nvml-err', e)
nvmlShutdown()
PY
```

sanjay: ops suggestion: when drain/replace is triggered, attach triage artifact to the node ticket and set label "gpu-fault:confirmed" if Xid in mapping. reduces back-and-forth.

leo: quick grep example to normalize mixed dmesg/journal formats: 
```bash
# normalize to timestamp + short message
journalctl -k --no-pager --utc | egrep "NVRM|Xid|GPU has" | sed -E 's/^\s*([0-9T:-]+) (.*)/\1 \2/' | tail -n200
```

maria: can infra-team own a tiny lambda that runs nightly to scan recent triage artifacts and surface nodes with >3 corrected ECC events in 24h? Cost low, helps prioritize replacers.

ashley: agreed. I'll draft a compact extractor script and a systemd service that runs on kernel oops to atomically collect these three things: 1) trimmed dmesg, 2) nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR snapshot, 3) nvml counters. output single gz with a .summary line.

sanjay: perfect. pls include tests for when journalctl is truncated (use /dev/kmsg fallback) and a fallback to copy /var/log/messages.

maria: thanks — can you drop a PR with script + runbook snippet? I'll review. :thumbsup:

ashley: will do this afternoon, linking back here when ready.

infra-bot: /triage-collect usage: /triage-collect <node> --since 15m --upload. Generated artifact: s3://redwood-gpu-triage/1805550000-gpu-234.tar.gz

leo: nice. small follow-up: include PCIe link state lines too, often shows 'link down' before Xid.

sanjay: added to runbook notes. closing loop once PR lands.
